tests: Counterparty exists but is never named: the seller's two edges extract, and the buyer's edge is DROPPED rather than stored against a placeholder node. Contrast fixture_04, where both parties are named and the untraversable edge is stored with status=denied instead.

predicates.OWNS_STAKE_IN: OWNS_STAKE_IN(holder, insurer). fields: stake_pct, status, start_date, end_date.
predicates.ACQUIRED: ACQUIRED(buyer, company_acquired). The object is ALWAYS the company whose control changed hands - never the seller, never the exiting JV partner, whatever the sentence is shaped like. Fires only when the reported event takes the buyer from no holding, or a holding of 50% or less, to a holding above 50% - control changing hands, which no single stake triple states. It does NOT fire when a buyer who already controls the company tops up (74 to 100, 51 to 71, 70 to 89): that end state is already carried by the OWNS_STAKE_IN triple, so an ACQUIRED triple there would be derivable and could only disagree with it. fields: status, start_date.
predicates.APPOINTED: APPOINTED(organisation, person). The organisation is always the subject; the direction is never reversed. fields: role, status, start_date, end_date.
predicates.DISTRIBUTES_FOR: DISTRIBUTES_FOR(distributor, insurer). A distribution tie-up is never ownership and never implies a stake. fields: status, start_date, end_date.

convention.temporal: start_date/end_date are four-digit years as integers. An absent end_date means the relation is still current as of the document's pub_date. Record a year only when the document states it or pub_date fixes it; never infer one from context.
convention.status: asserted | prospective | denied. Status is decided per triple, not per document: one document can carry an asserted background holding and a prospective deal at once.
convention.unstorable: A relation that must not be traversed is handled one of two ways, decided by whether its endpoints resolve. Both parties named: STORE the triple with status=denied - a denial is still a fact about two known nodes, and the graph needs it to answer 'did X buy Y?'. A party that cannot be resolved to a named entity ('an undisclosed sovereign wealth fund'): DROP the triple entirely - there is no node to anchor it. Never mint a placeholder, a null subject, or a descriptive pseudo-entity to carry a triple.
convention.numbers: Record percentages the document states. Never compute a residual, a post-deal holding, or a start year the text does not give.
convention.coverage: MERGED_WITH, PARTNERED_WITH and SUBSIDIARY_OF are specified in the extraction prompt and permitted by the schema, but no fixture covers them. Any of the three appearing in output for these eleven documents is a false positive.

expected_absent.node: undisclosed West Asian sovereign wealth fund
expected_absent.why: A description is not an entity; no node may be minted for it.
An edge with an unresolvable subject is dropped, not stored with a null or placeholder subject.
Do not split the insurer into a second node from the headline's short form.
10% does not cross 50%, and the buyer has no node in any case.
